Is the suspected or confirmed infection, condition, or clinical syndrome the primary reason for hospital admission?.  This refers to whether suspected or confirmed infection with the pathogen of interest if the reason (indication) for the hospital admission..

Case classification status, Options: Confirmed, Probable, Suspected, Discarded, Error.  Confirmed refers to a case that is laboratory confirmed and may fulfil the clinical criteria as described in the case definition. Probable refers to a clinically compatible illness that is epidemiologically linked to a confirmed case without laboratory confirmation of infection with pathogen of interest. Suspected refers to a clinically compatible illness without epidemiological link or laboratory confirmation. Discarded refers to a patient with a negative laboratory test and has failed to fulfil the criteria for a suspect, probable or confirmed case..

Reason for testing, Options: Symptomatic, Asymptomatic contact-traced, Asymptomatic mass testing campaign, t tested, Other.  This refers to the reason the patient was tested for the pathogen of interest..
Specify other reason.  This refers to the reason the patient was tested for the pathogen of interest..

This refers to provision of informed consent by the patient or their representative for participation in this study..
Date of consent.  This refers to date on which informed consent was given for the participants inclusion in this study..
Consent provided by, Options: Participant, Parent/guardian, Consultee, Independent clinician.  This refers to who provided the consent for participation in this study..

Does the child or young person give their assent?, Options: t competent.  This refers to assent given by a minor or adult who is unable to give consent on their own behalf, to participate in a study. Assent must be accompanied by consent from a parent or legal guardian for full participation in the study..

Was the patient admitted previously or transferred from any other facility during this illness episode?, Options: -admitted previously to this facility and discharged, -admitted to other facility and discharged, -admitted to ather facility then transferred to this facility.  This refers to previous admission to a health facility or transfer from another health facility during the current episode of illness..
Name of transfer facility.  This refers to the name of the facility from which the patient was previously admitted or transferred..
Date of presentation at previous facility.  This refers to the date of presentation to the facility at which the patient was previously admitted or transferred..

Specify other reason.  This refers to the reason for transfer from facility.
Total number of previous admissions for this infection.  This refers to the number of times (for this infection) the patient has been admitted to a health facility..

Date of earliest admission for this infection.  This refers to the date of the first admission for this illness. If the patient was first 'admitted to other facility, then transferred to this facility' record the date the patient was admitted to the other health facility..

Chronic neurological disorder.  Includes disorders of the brain, spinal cord, cranial nerves, peripheral nerves, nerve roots, autonomic nervous system, neuromuscular junction, and muscle. This can include any of cerebral palsy, multiple sclerosis, motor neurone disease, muscular dystrophy, myasthenia gravis, Parkinson's disease, stroke, and severe learning difficulty..
Epilepsy.  This refers to a disorder causing recurrent unprovoked seizures.

Dementia.  Defined as evidence from the history and mental status examination that indicates major impairment in learning and memory as well as impairment in at least one of the following: handling complex tasks; reasoning ability; spatial ability and orientation; language. The cognitive symptoms must significantly interfere with the individual's work performance, usual social activities, or relationships with other people. This must represent a significant decline from a previous level of functioning. The disturbances are not occurring exclusively during the course of delirium, and the disturbances are not better accounted for by a major psychiatric diagnosis. Chronic cognitive deficit is included..

Stroke / cerebrovascular accident.  Defined as a sudden loss of neurological function secondary to haemorrhage or ischemia in the brain parenchyma due to a vascular event. Stroke may be a clinical diagnosis, with or without supportive radiological findings..

Hemiplegia.  This refers to severe or complete loss of motor function on one side of the body; often caused by brain diseases that are localized to the cerebral hemisphere opposite to the side of weakness; less frequently, brain stem lesions; cervical spinal cord diseases, peripheral nervous system diseases, and other conditions may manifest as hemiplegia..
Paraplegia.  This refers to complete paralysis of the lower half of the body including both legs, often caused by damage to the spinal cord..
Cardiovascular comorbidities.  This refers to comorbidities relating to the cardiovascular system..

Chronic cardiac disease (not hypertension).  Defined as a disease that progressively causes deterioration of the heart and its functioning. This includes congenital heart diseases (e.g. tetralogy of fallot).

Myocardial infarction.  Defined as gross necrosis of the myocardium, as a result of interruption of the blood supply to the area, as in coronary thrombosis. This includes previous (history of) myocardial infarction..
Congestive heart failure.  Defined as failure of the heart to pump a sufficient amount of blood to meet the needs of the body tissues, resulting in tissue congestion and oedema..

Hypertension.  Defined as elevated arterial blood pressure diagnosed clinically (systolic blood pressure >140mmHg systolic and/or diastolic blood pressure >90mmHg), or for which a patient is prescribed an anti-hypertensive..

Peripheral vascular disease.  This refers to deviation from or interruption of the normal structure or function of the blood vessels outside the heart; diseases of the peripheral as opposed to the cardiac circulation..
Respiratory comorbidities.  This refers to comorbidities relating to the respiratory system..

Chronic pulmonary disease (not asthma).  Defined as any pulmonary condition other than asthma, that is a disease or disorder of slow progression and long duration which causes continuous or episodic periods of illness and/or incapacity..

Asthma.  This is defined as clinician-diagnosed asthma, a chronic airway disorder characterized by variable and recurring symptoms of airflow obstruction, bronchial hyper-responsiveness, and/or underlying inflammation. Current pharmaceutical intervention - for prevention or treatment of symptoms - is not a pre-requisite for the inclusion of this diagnosis..
Gastrointestinal comorbidities.  This refers to comorbidities relating to the gastrointestinal system..

Peptic ulcer disease.  This refers to acid peptic injury of the digestive tract, resulting in mucosal break reaching the submucosa. Peptic ulcers are usually located in the stomach or proximal duodenum, but they can also be found in the oesophagus or Meckel's diverticulum..
Liver disease.  Defined as any disorder of the hepatobiliary system. Manifestations may include signs and symptoms of cholestasis, portal hypertension, and/or abnormal liver function tests..

Type of liver disease, Options: Mild, Moderate or severe.  Defined as mild - chronic hepatitis or cirrhosis without portal hypertension, and moderate or severe - cirrhosis with portal hypertension, with or without bleeding or a history of variceal bleeding..
Renal / Genitourinary comorbidities.  This refers to comorbidities relating to the renal / genitourinary system..

Chronic kidney disease.  This is defined as a clinician-diagnosed chronic kidney disease (CKD, also known as chronic kidney failure). The KDIGO and KDOQI definition of chronic kidney disease is kidney damage for 3 months, as defined by structural or functional abnormalities of the kidney, with or without decreased glomerular filtration rate (GFR), that can lead to decreased GFR, manifest by either: Pathologic abnormalities; or Markers of kidney damage, including abnormalities in the composition of the blood or urine, or abnormalities in imaging tests; or GFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m^2 for 3 months, with or without kidney damage..

Stage of chronic kidney disease, Options: Stage, Stage, Stage a, Stage b, Stage, Stage.  This refers to the stage of chronic kidney disease (CKD) based on estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). CKD Stages: 1 - Kidney damage, normal eGFR (90ml/min); 2 - Kidney damage, mild GFR decrease (60-89ml/min); 3a - Moderate GFR decrease (45-59ml/min); 3b - Moderate to severe GFR decrease (30-44ml/min); 4 - Severe GFR decrease (15-29ml/min); 5 - Kidney failure (<15ml/min or on dialysis)..
Infectious comorbidities.  This refers to infection-related comorbidities..

HIV.  Defined as a person living with laboratory-confirmed Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) 1 or 2 infection, or a patient with an Acquired Immunity Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS) defining illness. This is irrespective of the CD4 lymphocyte count/percentage or HIV viral load in blood. ART refers to anti-retroviral therapy and is distinct from pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) or post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP)..

Is the patient on anti-retroviral therapy (ART)?.  Anti-retroviral therapy (ART) refers to drug therapy, for patients with HIV infection, which targets retrovirus function by multiple mechanisms to aggressively suppress HIV replication. It is distinct from pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) or post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP)..

Specify ART.  This refers to antiretroviral therapy (ART) used in treatment of HIV infections with medications that target the virus directly, limiting the ability of infected cells to produce new virus particles. It is distinct from pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) or post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP)..
If HIV positive: CD4 count date.  This refers to the date of the most recent laboratory-based CD4 cell count available..
If HIV positive: Most recent CD4 count (cells/µL).  This refers to the date of the most recent laboratory-based CD4 cell count available..

If HIV positive: Is HIV viral load detectable.  Detectable typically includes suppressed (detected but <= 1000 copies/mL) and unsuppressed (>1000 copies/mL). Undetectable refers to viral load not detected by test used..
Most recent HIV viral load (copies/mL).  Defined as the most recent laboratory-based HIV viral load available expressed in copies/mL..
HIV viral load date.  This refers to the date of the most recent laboratory-based HIV viral load available..

Tuberculosis.  Defined as patients currently receiving treatment for tuberculosis, an infection caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Latent tuberculosis should not be included here. Patients who have been cured of tuberculosis should not be included here. Those who have chronic pulmonary sequelae following their tuberculosis should be included as chronic pulmonary disease..

Specify tuberculosis type, Options: Active pulmonary, Active extra-pulmonary.  This refers to the type of Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection. Active pulmonary TB refers to bacterial infection that affects the lungs and is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, with signs and symptoms including chronic cough with blood-tinged sputum, night sweats, fever, fatigue, and weight loss. Active extra-pulmonary TB refers to Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection involving organs other than the lungs (e.g., pleura, lymph nodes, abdomen, genitourinary tract, skin, joints and bones, or meninges). Latent TB refers to the asymptomatic presence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in the body, which is determined by a positive result to a tuberculin skin test or interferon-gamma release assay..

Latent tuberculosis.  This refers to the asymptomatic presence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in the body, which is determined by a positive result to a tuberculin skin test or interferon-gamma release assay..
Previous tuberculosis.  This refers to previous history of active tuberculosis infection, irrespective of treatment status and disease outcome of previous infection.
Chronic hepatitis B/C infection.  Defined as chronic hepatitis due to infection by hepatitis B (HBV) or hepatitis C (HCV) virus. Do not include those with a documented cure of hepatitis C..
Haematological comorbidities.  This refers to comorbidities relating to the haematological system..

Chronic haematologic disease.  This refers to chronic disorders of the blood and blood forming tissues. Examples include Polycythemia Vera, Myelodysplastic Syndromes (MDS). Does not include leukaemia, lymphoma or myeloma, which should be entered under malignancy. Does not include iron-deficiency anaemia which is explained by diet or chronic blood loss..
Blood transfusion in last month.  This refers to a history of previous blood transfusion within the past month of a calendar year..
Sickle cell disease.  This refers to a genetic blood disorder characterized by the appearance of sickle-shaped red blood cells and anemia..
Systemic / general comorbidities.  This refers to systemic / general comorbidities..

Rheumatologic disorder.  Defined as an disorders of connective tissue, especially the joints and related structures characterised by inflammation, degeneration or metabolic derangement. It includes chronic arthropathies and arthritis, connective tissue disorders and vasculitides..

Specify  Rheumatologic disorder, Options: Osteoarthritis, Rheumatoid Arthritis, Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, Ankylosing Spondylitis, Psoriatic Arthritis, Other.  This refers to rheumatologic disorders. Osteoarthritis is a disabling joint disease characterized by degeneration of the joint complex that can have various causes, most notably advanced age and overuse. Rheumatoid Arthritis is a chronic, systemic autoimmune disorder characterized by inflammation in the synovial membranes and articular surfaces. Systemic Lupus Erythematosus is a chronic, relapsing, inflammatory, and often febrile multisystemic disorder of connective tissue, characterized principally by involvement of the skin, joints, kidneys, and serosal membranes. Ankylosing Spondylitis is a chronic inflammatory disease of the axial skeleton that leads to partial or complete vertebral fusion and spine rigidity. Psoriatic Arthritis is a seronegative inflammatory arthritis found in patients with psoriasis..
Specify  Other Rheumatologic disorder.  This refers to rheumatologic disorders. .

Asplenia.  Defined as the anatomical absence of the spleen or functional asplenia secondary to a variety of disease states. This can include congenital absence (born without a spleen), or acquired absence, for example secondary to surgical removal..
Benign neoplasm.  This refers to a neoplasm characterized by the absence of atypical or malignant cytological and architectural features, and absence of invasive features or metastatic potential..

Malignant neoplasm.  Defined as a tumour composed of atypical neoplastic, often pleomorphic cells that invade other tissues. Includes haematological malignancies, that are considered to be biologically active. The most common malignant neoplasms are carcinomas (adenocarcinomas or squamous cell carcinomas), Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphomas, leukaemias, melanomas, and sarcomas. It specifically does not include malignancies that have been cured or where there is no evidence of on-going disease relating to that malignancy following treatment..

Malignant solid neoplasm.  Defined as a malignant neoplasm arising from solid tissues that do not include fluid areas (e.g., blood or bone marrow). Representative examples include carcinomas (adenocarcinomas or squamous cell carcinomas) and sarcomas. Hematopoietic and lymphoid tissue malignancies are not considered solid neoplasms and are covered as leukaemia and lymphoma below..

Leukemia.  Defined as a progressive, malignant disease of the blood-forming organs, characterized by distorted proliferation and development of leukocytes and their precursors in the blood and bone marrow. Leukemias were originally termed acute or chronic based on life expectancy but now are classified according to cellular maturity..

Lymphoma.  Defined as a malignant (clonal) proliferation of B- lymphocytes or T- lymphocytes which involves the lymph nodes, bone marrow and/or extranodal sites. This category includes Non-Hodgkin lymphomas and Hodgkin lymphomas..
Obesity.  Refers to body weight grossly above recommended standard. BMI >= 30 kg/m2 or other locally appropriate BMI cut off can be used to define obesity..

Malnutrition.  This refers to any clinically identified deficiency in intake, either of total energy or of specific nutrients, that led to a dietetic intervention or referral prior to this admission..

Diabetes mellitus.  Defined as a metabolic disorder characterized by abnormally high blood sugar levels due to diminished production of insulin or insulin resistance or desensitization. This includes Type 1 diabetes mellitus, Type 2 diabetes mellitus, or Gestational diabetes (during previous pregnancy) requiring oral or subcutaneous treatment..

Diabetes mellitus type, Options: Type, Type, Gestational diabetes.  Refers to a subtype of diabetes mellitus that is characterized by insulin deficiency; it is manifested by the sudden onset of severe hyperglycemia, rapid progression to diabetic ketoacidosis, and death unless treated with insulin; the disease may occur at any age, but is most common in childhood or adolescence..

End organ damage from diabetes.  Refers to irreparable damage to multiple organs/systems which is the result of chronic complications of diabetes. The affected organs/systems include the cardiovascular system, kidneys, eyes, nervous system, joints and feet..

HbA1C result within last 6 months.  Haemoglobin A1C (HbA1C) is a blood test that measures average blood glucose level over the three months preceding the test result. It can be reported in different units (mmol/mol or %)..

Alcohol dependency.  This refers to a pattern of alcohol use that causes significant physical and psychosocial impairment or distress..
Intravenous drug user.  This refers to a disorder causing recurrent unprovoked seizures.

Primary immunodeficiency.  This refers to immunodeficiency disease that arises independent of another pathologic process, disease, or injury..
Chemotherapy.  This refers to treatment that uses drugs to stop the growth of cancer cells, either by killing the cells or by stopping them from dividing..
Radiation therapy.  This refers to the use of high-energy radiation from x-rays, gamma rays, neutrons, protons, and other sources to kill cancer cells and shrink tumors..

Long term or high-dose corticosteroid therapy.  This refers to use of exogenous corticosteroids in high-doses or for long term (typically for over 4 weeks) periods for the treatment of any disease or disorder..

Relevant skin condition(s) (atopic dermatitis or active exfoliative skin conditions).  This refers to any deviation from the normal structure or function of the skin or subcutaneous tissue that is manifested by a characteristic set of symptoms and signs..

Describe the skin condition(s).  This refers to any deviation from the normal structure or function of the skin or subcutaneous tissue that is manifested by a characteristic set of symptoms and signs..

Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (cm).  This refers to an anthropometric measure of the circumference of the upper arm at the midpoint between the shoulder and elbow..

Prematurity (<37 weeks).  This refers to a live birth between 20 weeks' and 37 weeks' gestation..
Congenital Immunodeficiency.  This refers to a congenital deficiency or defect in one or more of the main components of the immune system..

Active Infections and Recent Risk Factors.  .
Active chickenpox.  This refers to an active chickenpox infection caused by varicella zoster virus. .
Active measles.  This refers to active measles (rubeola) infection caused by the measles virus..

Active shingles (herpes zoster).  This refers to an active case of shingles or herpes zoster dues to the reactivation of the varicella-zoster virus that has remained dormant, after the patient's initial exposure to the virus in the form of varicella (chickenpox)..
Active Hepatitis C.  This refers to an active case of hepatitis C virus infection..
Active Hepatitis B.  This refers to an active case of hepatitis B virus infection..
Active Mumps.  This refers to an active mumps infection, which transmitted via infectious respiratory particles and primarily affects children, caused by mumps virus..
Active Zika.  This refers to an active zika infection caused by zika virus..
Active Dengue.  This refers to an active dengue infection caused by dengue virus.
Active Enterovirus.  This refers to an active infection caused by viruses in the enterovirus genus, including poliovirus, Coxsackie A and B, and rhinovirus. .
Active Polio.  This refers to an active infection caused by poliovirus.

Indication / reason, Options: Shock, High/rising haematocrit, Arexia, Persistent vomiting, Other.  This refers to the indication for intravenous fluids. Shock refers to circulatory failure, causing inadequate oxygen delivery to meet cellular metabolic needs. It is characterised by any two of the following: evidence of hypoperfusion (e.g. slow capillary refill, cold skin, and rapid and weak pulse), narrow pulse pressure (less than or equal to 20mmHg), hypotension for age, and tachycardia..

Select all blood products that were administered., Options: Platelets, Cryoprecipitate, Whole blood, Frozen fresh plasma, Fibrigen concentrate, Packed RBC (red cell concentrate).  Platelets refers to the transfer of blood platelets from a donor to a recipient or reinfusion to the donor. Cryoprecipitate refers to a frozen blood product prepared from frozen plasma that contains fibrinogen (factor I), antihemophilic factor (factor VIII), factor XIII, von Willebrand factor (vWF) and fibronectin. Whole blood refers to intravenous administration of whole blood (blood that contains plasma and red blood cells) into an individual. Packed RBC refers to red blood cells from a unit of whole blood following removal of most of the plasma, leaving a unit with a haematocrit of about 6%. Fresh frozen plasma refers to the plasma that is separated from the whole blood and frozen quickly after a blood donation in order to be used for blood transfusions. Fibrinogen concentrate is a haemostatic agent used for the treatment of acute bleeding episodes in patients with congenital fibrinogen deficiency, including afibrinogenemia and hypofibrinogenemia..

Antihypertensives.  This refers to any substance used in the treatment of acute or chronic hypertension regardless of pharmacological mechanism. Examples include: ACE Inhibitors (Lisinopril (Zestril), Enalapril (Vasotec), Ramipril (Altace), Captopril); Angiotensin Receptor Blockers ((Losartan (Cozaar), Valsartan (Diovan), Irbesartan (Avapro), Olmesartan (Benicar)); Beta-Blockers (Metoprolol (Lopressor), Carvedilol (Coreg), Bisoprolol, Atenolol); Calcium Channel Blockers (Amlodipine (Norvasc), Diltiazem (Cardizem), Verapamil); Diuretics (Furosemide (Lasix), Spironolactone (Aldactone), Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ)).

Antidiabetic medications.  This refers to any substance used to reduce hyperglycemia or treat disorders associated with diabetes. Examples include: Metformin (Glucophage); SGLT2 Inhibitors (Empagliflozin (Jardiance), Dapagliflozin (Farxiga), Canagliflozin (Invokana)); DPP-4 Inhibitors (Sitagliptin (Januvia), Linagliptin (Tradjenta), Saxagliptin (Onglyza)); GLP-1 Receptor Agonists (Liraglutide (Victoza), Semaglutide (Ozempic), Dulaglutide (Trulicity)); Insulins (Glargine (Lantus), Aspart (NovoLog), Lispro (Humalog), Detemir (Levemir)).

Lipid-lowering drugs.  This refers to any substance used to lower the levels of certain lipids in the blood in the treatment of hyperlipidaemias. Examples include: Statins (Atorvastatin (Lipitor), Rosuvastatin (Crestor), Simvastatin (Zocor), Pravastatin (Pravachol)); Ezetimibe (Zetia).

Anti-reflux or other GI medications.  This refers to any substance used in the treatment gastric reflux by preventing the backward flow of stomach acid contents into the esophagus, or other drugs taken for ailments of the gastrointestinal system. Examples include: Proton Pump Inhibitors (Omeprazole (Prilosec), Pantoprazole (Protonix), Esomeprazole (Nexium), Lansoprazole (Prevacid)); H2-Receptor Antagonists (Ranitidine (Zantac), Famotidine (Pepcid)).

Antidepressants and Anxiolytics.  Antidepressants refers to mood-stimulating drugs used primarily in the treatment of affective disorders and related conditions. Anxiolytics refers to drugs used to treat anxiety disorders. Examples include: Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors (Sertraline (Zoloft), Citalopram (Celexa), Fluoxetine (Prozac), Escitalopram (Lexapro)); Serotonin-Norepinephrine Reuptake Inhibitors (Venlafaxine (Effexor), Duloxetine (Cymbalta)); Benzodiazepines (Lorazepam (Ativan), Diazepam (Valium), Alprazolam (Xanax)).

Antiepileptics.  This refers to any substance used stop, prevent, or control seizures (convulsions). Examples include: Levetiracetam (Keppra), Valproate (Depakote), Carbamazepine (Tegretol), Lamotrigine (Lamictal)..

Systemic / general symptoms.  This refers to systemic / general / non-specific signs and symptoms.
Fever.  This refers to sensation of elevated body temperature without formal measurement, or a measured body temperature greater or equal to 38-degrees Celsius (38°C) or 100.4-Fahrenheit (100.4°F)..
Number of days before presentation to hospital:.  This refers to the number of days this symptom persisted before presentation to hospital.
Resolution of fever (if resolved) days before presentation:.  This refers to the number of days before presentation to the hospital that the symptom resolved..
Chills or rigors.  This refers to severe chills with violent shivering. A rigor is an episode of shaking or exaggerated shivering which can occur with a high fever..
Night sweats.  This refers to perspiration experienced nocturnally that is unrelated to environmental temperature..
Cold sweats.  This refers to sweats accompanied by sensation of feeling cold, different from sweats caused by heat or exertion..
Excessive sweating (hyperhidrosis).  This refers to excessive sweating that is not always related to fever, heat exposure or vigorous exercise..

Restlessness.  This refers to a state of unease, characterised by an inability to rest or relax, diffuse motor activity with limited control, nonproductive or disorganized behaviour, and subjective distress..

Fatigue / malaise / lethargy.  This refers to a constellation of non-specific sensations: the feeling of tiredness characterised by a lack of energy or motivation; general discomfort or uneasiness; disinterestedness, listlessness, and indifference, resulting in difficulty performing simple tasks or concentrating..
Weakness.  This refers  to a decrease in muscle strength..

Weight loss.  This refers to reduction in total body weight (patient-reported or objectively measured) that has occurred since the onset of this illness and has been unintentional or not attributable to active dieting, exercise or dedicated medication based weight-loss interventions..
Loss of smell (anosmia).  This refers to patient reported and/or clinician-diagnosed inability of the patient to perceive odours.
Loss of taste (ageusia).  This refers to patient reported and/or clinician-diagnosed loss of taste function of the tongue..
Feeling dizzy / faint.  This refers to the subjective feeling of light-headedness or dizziness which may precede an episode of syncope or a sensation of unsteadiness, spinning or rocking..
Muscle aches (myalgia).  This refers to pain localised to a muscle or group of muscles..
Myalgia intensity (Numeric Pain Rating Scale).  This refers to the intensity of the muscle pain (myalgia), as reported on the numeric pain rating scale from 1 (lowest) to 10 (highest)..
Joint pain (arthralgia).  This refers to a sensation of marked discomfort or pain localised to one or more joints, including small and big joints..
Artralgia intensity (Numeric Pain Rating Scale).  This refers to the intensity of the joint pain (arthralgia), as reported on the numeric pain rating scale from 1 (lowest) to 10 (highest)..
Site where joint pain occurred, Options: Shoulder, Elbow, Wrist, Small joints of hand, Knee, Ankle, Small joints of foot, Other.  This refers to the sites where the joint pain occurred..
How many shoulder joints are affected?.  This refers to the number of shoulder joints affected.
How many elbow joints are affected?.  This refers to the number of elbow joints affected..
How many wrist joints are affected?.  This refers to the number of wrist joints affected..
How many knee joints are affected?.  This refers to the number of knee joints affected..
How many ankle joints are affected?.  This refers to the number of ankle joints affected..

Joint swelling.  Defined as the buildup of fluid in the soft tissue SURROUNDING the joint or in the joint itself.
Site where joint swelling occurred, Options: Shoulder, Elbow, Wrist, Small joints of hand, Knee, Ankle, Small joints of foot, Other.  This refers to the location where joint swelling first occurred.

Joint stiffness.  This refers to a constellation of non-specific sensations: the feeling of tiredness characterised by a lack of energy or motivation; general discomfort or uneasiness; disinterestedness, listlessness, and indifference, resulting in difficulty performing si.
Stiffness NRS - Patient-reported (0-10).  This refers to the patient reported rating of joint stiffenss on a numerical rating scale from 1 (least) to 10 (worst).
Morning stiffness duration (min).  This refers to duration of joint stiffness in the morning (in minutes).
Joint tenderness.  Defined as pain and discomfort in a joint, often accompanied by sensitivity to touch.
Site where joint tenderness occurred, Options: Fingers, Wrists, Shoulders, Elbow, Hips, Knees, Ankles, Toes, Other.  This refers to the location where joint tenderness first occurred.
Specify other first joint tenderness location.  This refers to the location where joint tenderness first occurred.
Small tissue swelling.  Defined as painful swelling of the interphalangeal tissue, leading to tension and pain when flexing the fingers.
Back Pain.  This refers to painful sensation in the posterior regions of the thorax and lumbosacrum or the adjacent regions..
Neck Pain.  This refers to painful sensation in the neck region..

Skin rash.  This refers to any change in the skin which affects its appearance or texture. A rash may be localized to one part of the body or affect all the skin. Rashes may cause the skin to change colour, itch, become warm, bumpy, dry, cracked, or blistered, swell and may be painful..

Site where rash first occurred, Options: Skin genital, Skin n-genital, Mucosa genital, Mucosa n-genital, Mouth, Perianal skin, Rectum, Other.  This refers to the location where the rash first occurred..
Specify other first rash location.  This refers to the location where the rash first occurred..
Date first rash was observed by patient.  This refers to the date the patient reports to have first identified the rash..
Skin paresthesia.  This refers to percieved cutaneous sensations (e.g., cold, warmth, tingling, pressure, etc.) that are experienced spontaneously in the absence of stimulation..
Changes in skin texture.  This refers to alterations in the surface appearance and feel of the skin, such as roughness, unevenness, or the presence of bumps..
Skin pallor.  This refers to unnatural pale appearance of the skin..

Itch (pruritus).  Defined as an unpleasant or intense itching sensation that produces the urge to rub or scratch the skin to obtain relief. Itching is an irritating sensation that makes you want to scratch your skin..
Change in mobility from baseline.  This refers to the patient's ability to walk or mobilise..
Mobility status, Options: Fully ambulant, Ambulant but with some assistance, Bedridden.  This refers to the patient's ability to walk or mobilise..

Sleeping more than usual / lethargic / sluggish / listlessness.  This refers to excessive sleepiness during the daytime / marked by drowsiness and an unusual lack of energy and mental alertness / infant having little energy, is drowsy, or sleeps more than usual.
Increased thirst (polydipsia).  This refers to excessive thirst.
Changes in menstruation / Irregular menstruation.  This refers to any deviations from the normal process; e.g. delayed, difficult, profuse, scanty, unusual bleeding, etc..
Respiratory symptoms.  This refers to signs and symptoms relating to the respiratory system..

Cough.  This refers to the presence of a cough and its characteristics. A productive cough refers to a cough accompanied by expectorated secretions (phlegm or mucus), while a non-productive cough refers to one which is not accompanied by expectorated secretions. Haemoptysis refers to the presence of blood or blood-streaked sputum from the respiratory tract..
Cough type, Options: n Productive, Productive, Haemoptysis.  This refers to the type of cough. A productive cough refers to a cough accompanied by expectorated secretions (phlegm or mucus).
Coryza.  This refers to inflammation of the nasal mucosa.
Sore throat.  Defined as an unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) and perceived to originate in the throat..
Runny nose (rhinorrhoea).  Defined as increased mucosal discharge of the nose..
Wheezing.  Defined as a high-pitched breath sound resulting from a narrowing or obstruction of the small airway..
Shortness of breath.  Defined as the uncomfortable sensation of difficult or laboured breathing that is out of proportion to the patient's level of physical activity..
Nasal congestion.  Defined as reduced ability to pass air through the nasal cavity often leading to mouth breathing..
Chest pain.  Defined as the unpleasant, uncomfortable or painful sensation characterised by physical discomfort localised to the chest..
Sneezing.  This refers to a sudden violent, spasmodic, audible expiration of breath through the nose and mouth..
Hiccups.  This refers to a quick, involuntary contraction of the diaphragm, which leads to inspiration and an audible, reflexive closure of the vocal cords. .
Cardiovascular symptoms.  This refers to signs and symptoms relating to the cardiovascular system..
Palpitations.  Refers to the unpleasant awareness of one's own heartbeat..
Gastrointestinal symptoms.  This refers to signs and symptoms relating to the gastrointestinal system..
Abdominal pain.  Defined as an unpleasant sensation of discomfort, distress or agony in the abdominal region..
Diarrhoea.  Defined as abnormally increased frequency (usually defined as three or more) loose or liquid bowel movement per day (or more frequent passage than is normal for the individual)..
Number of episodes of diarrhoea in past 24 hours.  Refers to the number of diarrhoeal episodes experienced in the past 24 hours..
Constipation.  Defined as irregular and infrequent or difficult evacuation of the bowels..
Vomiting.  Defined as the expulsion of the stomach or small intestines through the mouth..
Persistent vomiting? (>=2/day).  This refers to persistent vomiting, defined here as vomiting two times or more per day..
Vomiting blood (haematemesis).  This refers to vomiting of blood..
Nausea.  Defined as the the unpleasant painless subjective feeling that one will imminently vomit..
Anorexia.  Defined as lack or loss of appetite..
Excessive salivation.  Defined as excessive salivation or sialorrhea, is a symptom best assessed by the patient..
Difficulty swallowing (dysphagia).  Defined as difficulty swallowing food, liquids, or saliva..
Faecal incontinence.  Defined as failure of voluntary control of the anal sphincters, with involuntary passage of feces and flatus..
Renal / Genitourinary symptoms.  This refers to signs and symptoms relating to the renal / genitourinary system..
Urinary retention.  Defined as the accumulation of urine within the bladder because of the inability to urinate..
Urinary incontinence.  This refers to loss of bladder control, or being unable to control urination..
Increased urination (polyuria).  This refers to excessive or frequent urination..
Pain during urination (dysuria).  This refers to painful or difficult urination..
Painful intercourse (dyspareunia).  Defined as recurrent or persistent genital pain associated with sexual intercourse..
Haematological symptoms.  This refers to signs and symptoms relating to the haematological system..

Bleeding (haemorrhage).  Defined as the presence of blood in a location in which it is not physiologically normal or loss of blood from the circulation, either internally or externally. This can include epistaxis (blood from nose), gingival bleeding (blood from gums/gingiva), blood from any part of the gastrointestinal tract (gastrointestinal bleeding) or genitourinary tracts (vagina or urethra) including hematuria..
Severe bleeding (requires intervention).  Defined as the severe bleeding / hemorrhage requiring medical intervention for hemostasis and/or hemodynamic support..
Specify bleeding site(s).  This refers to the location of bleeding/haemorrhage site(s)..

Specify other bleeding / haemorrhage site(s).  This refers to the location of bleeding/haemorrhage site(s). Petechiae refer to small reddish or purplish spots in skin or mucous membrane as a result of localised haemorrhage. Nose bleeding refers to haemorrhage localized in the nose. Gum bleeding refers to haemorrhage affecting the gingiva. Gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding refers to haemorrhage in any segment of the gastrointestinal tract from oesophagus to rectum. Urinary tract bleeding refers to haemorrhage originating from any part of the urinary system. Vaginal bleeding refers to haemorrhage originating from vagina, unrelated to normal menstruation..
Neurological symptoms.  This refers to signs and symptoms relating to the neurological system..
Headache.  Defined as the experience of pain in various parts of the head..
Number of days before presentation:.  This refers to the number of days this symptom persisted before presentation to hospital.
Photophobia.  Refers to increased sensitivity of the eyes to light..

Seizures / convulsions.  Defined as an intermittent abnormality of nervous system physiology characterised by a transient occurrence of sudden, violent, irregular movement of the body, caused by involuntary contraction of muscles due to abnormal excessive or synchronous neuronal activity in the brain..
Altered consciousness / confusion.  Defined as a level of awareness or arousal other than the patient's normal baseline..
Focal weakness.  This refers to impairments of brain function, the nerve or spinal cord that affect a specific region of the body..
Paralysis.  This refers to inability to fully move or control movement.
Irritability.  Refers to an abnormal or excessive excitability with easily triggered anger, annoyance, or impatience..
Tremor.  Refers to an unintentional, oscillating to-and-fro muscle movement about a joint axis..
Difficulty in walking.  This refers to any persistent problem with walking..

Personality changes (includes, agitation, psychosis, somnolence, insomnia, catatonia, mood lability, altered sleep pattern and in children, new onset enuresis, or irritability).  This refers to a new or worsening change in the patient's usual behaviour, mood, or mental state, including agitation, psychosis, somnolence, insomnia, catatonia, mood lability, altered sleep pattern, and, in children, new-onset enuresis or irritability..
Abnormal movement .  This refers to a new or worsening change in a voluntary of involuntary movement experienced by the patient.

Specify:, Options: Chorea, Athetosis, Dystonia, Hemiballismus, Stereotypies, Orolingual dyskinesia, Tic.  This refers to the type of abnormal movement. Chorea: Involuntary, irregular, rapid, non-rhythmic movements that appear to flow randomly from one body part to another. Athetosis: Involuntary, slow, continuous, writhing movements, typically affecting the hands, fingers, feet, or toes. Dystonia: Sustained or intermittent involuntary muscle contractions causing abnormal, often repetitive movements or postures. Hemiballismus: Involuntary, large-amplitude, violent flinging movements affecting one side of the body. Stereotypies: Repetitive, purposeless, patterned movements or vocalizations that are performed in the same way each time. Orolingual dyskinesia: Involuntary, repetitive movements of the mouth, lips, jaw, or tongue. Tic: Sudden, rapid, recurrent, non-rhythmic motor movements or vocalizations that are difficult to suppress..
Other neurological symptoms.  This refers the presence of an alternative neurological abnormality not listed above..
Specify other neurological symptoms.  This refers the presence of another neurological abnormality not listed above..
Ophthalmological symptoms.  This refers to signs and symptoms relating to the eye..
Itching of eye(s).  Defined as itching of one or both eyes..
Red / Pink eye(s).  Defined as inflammation or infection of the conjunctiva, characterized by redness in one or both eyes..
Pain in eye(s).  Defined as discomfort or aching localized within or around the eye area..
Oedema of eyelid(s).  Defined as swelling due to fluid accumulation in the tissues of the eyelid..
Discharge from eye(s).  Defined as the release of fluids ranging from clear to pus-like from the eye, often indicative of infection or irritation..
Hazy / Blurred vision.  Defined as a loss of visual acuity, resulting in unclear or distorted sight..
Sensitivity of eye to light.  Defined as an abnormal intolerance to light, causing discomfort or pain in the eyes when exposed to bright light..
Visual disturbance.  Refers to an interference to normal eyesight without necessarily affecting visual acuity..
Other opthalmological symptoms.  This refers to other signs and symptoms relating to the eye, not specified above..
Specify other opthalmological symptoms.  This refers to other signs and symptoms relating to the eye, not specified above..
Ear/Nose/Throat symptoms.  This refers to signs and symptoms relating to the ear, nose and throat..
Ear pain.  This refers to painful sensation in the ear.
Tinnitus.  This refers to an abnormal perception of sounds experienced by an individual in the absence of auditory stimulation..
Parotitis.  This refers to inflammation of the parotid glands..
Paediatric-specific symptoms.  .
Continuous crying.  This refers to uncontrolled episodes of crying occur without any apparent motivating stimuli. .
Feeding difficulty.  This refers to an impaired ability to eat related to problems gathering food and getting ready to suck, chew, or swallow it .
Other symptoms.  .
Other symptom(s).  This refers to the presence of an alternative sign or abnormality not listed above..
Systemic / general signs.  This refers to systemic / general / non-specific signs and symptoms.
Hypothermia.  This refers to abnormally reduced body temperature due to failed thermoregulation..
Cold / clammy peripheries.  This refers to skin that feels cool and moist to the touch, often associated with circulatory failure and symptoms like restlessness and hypotension..
Dehydration.  This refers to excessive loss of water from the body..
Dehydration Status, Options: Mild, Moderate, Severe.  This refers to excessive loss of water from the body..
Oedema.  This refers to accumulation of an excessive amount of fluid in cells or intercellular tissues..
Oedema site(s), Options: Feet, Ankle, Legs (below knee), Legs (above knees), Scrotum/Labia, Sacrum, Abdomen, Neck, Face, Other.  This refers to the location of the odema..
Specify other oedema site(s).  This refers to the location of the odema..
Lymphadenopathy, Options: -painful, -t painful.  Defined as a clinical finding of abnormal enlargement of the lymph nodes..
Specify lymphadenopathy site(s), Options: Axillary (arm pits), Cervical (neck), Inguinal (groin), Other.  This refers to the location in which lymphadenopathy was identified..
Specify other lymphadenopathy site(s).  This refers to the location in which lymphadenopathy was identified..
Bruising.  This refers to spontaneous extravasation of blood into the subcutaneous space, also referred to as spontaneous ecchymoses..
Pressure injury to skin.  This refers to a condition of localized tissue damage due to pressure that obstructs blood flow to the skin and subcutaneous tissue..
Alopecia.  This refers to absence of hair (nonscarring hair loss) from areas where it is normally present..
Dry skin.  This refers to skin characterized by the lack of natural or normal moisture resulting from inadequate hydrolipids in the skin, also called xerosis cutis..

Oral ulcers.  This refers to recurrent episodes of ulceration of the oral mucosa (recurrent oral aphthae), typically presenting as painful, sharply circumscribed fibrin-covered mucosal defects with a h.
Mastitis.  Defined as a inflammation of the breast, with or without accompanying infection.
Bacterial super-infection.  Defined as a physician-diagnosed secondary bacterial infection that occurs during an existing wound, infection or immediately following an earlier infection..

Specify bacterial super-infection., Options: Deep tissue abscess, Folliculitis / cellulitis, Pneumonia, Gastroenteritis, CNS, Bacteraemia, Urinary tract, Other.  This refers to the type or location of the bacterial super-infection..
Specify other bacterial super-infection.  This refers to the other type(s) or location(s) of the bacterial super-infection, not specified above..
Respiratory signs.  This refers to signs and symptoms relating to the respiratory system..
Respiratory distress.  This refer to a pathological increase in the effort and frequency of breathing movements..

Lower chest wall indrawing.  Defined as a clinical sign of respiratory distress, distinguished by the abnormal inward movement of the lower chest wall during inspiration. If only the soft tissue between the ribs or above the clavicle goes in when the patient breathes, this is not lower chest wall in-drawing..
Fast breathing (tachypnoea).  Defined as an abnormal increase of rate of breathing..
Apnoea.  Defined as a transient absence in spontaneous respiration..
Rhinitis.  Defined as inflammation of the mucous membrane lining the nose, usually associated with nasal discharge..
Pharyngitis.  This refers to the presence of inflammation of the throat...
Pharyngeal erythema.  This refers to an inflammatory redness of the phayngeal mucosa.
Pharyngeal exudate.  This refers to the presence of inflammatory exudative fluid e.g. pus on the pharygeal mucosa.
Tonsillitis.  This refers to the presence of inflammation of the tonsils..
Pleural effusion.  This refers to presence of fluid in the pleural cavity resulting from excessive transudation or exudation from the pleural surfaces..
Cardiovascular signs.  This refers to signs and symptoms relating to the cardiovascular system..
Rapid heart rate (tachycardia).  Refers to an abnormally rapid heart rate (typically > 100bpm for adults), that exceeds the range of the normal resting heart rate for age..
Cardiac arrhythmia.  Refers to an abnormality in rhythm of heartbeat, including rate, regularity, and/or sequence of activation abnormalities.
Peripheral cyanosis.  This refers to a condition of localized tissue damage due to pressure that obstructs blood flow to the skin and subcutaneous tissue..
Gastrointestinal signs.  This refers to signs and symptoms relating to the gastrointestinal system..
Ascites.  Defined as an excessive accumulation or retention of free fluid within the peritoneal cavity..
Palpable liver/Hepatomegaly.  Defined as an pathological enlargement of the liver.
Palpable spleen/splenomegaly.  Defined as an pathological enlargement of the spleen.
Tender abdomen.  This refers to painful sensation elicited upon touching the abdomen.
Jaundice.  Defined as a clinical manifestation of hyperbilirubinemia, characterized by the yellowish staining of the skin, mucous membrane and/or sclera..
Feeding.  This refers to whether the patient is feeding or not.
If yes, specify feeding route, Options: Oral, Feeding tube, Breastfeeding.  If feeding, this refers to the route of feeding.
If no, nil per oral (NPO) order?.  This refers to clinical orders to indicate that nothing (e.g., medications, food) should be taken by mouth..
Dark / tarry blood in faeces (melaena).  This refers to abnormally dark tarry feces containing blood, usually from gastrointestinal bleeding..

Fresh blood in stools (haematochezia).  This refers to the presence of blood in stool. It is the result of gastrointestinal hemorrhage and it may be easily seen in stool or may be identified microscopically..
Rectal bleeding.  This refers to bleeding originating from the rectal wall and discharged from the anus..
Reduced urine output.  This refers to a finding indicating that the urine production is less than 500 milliliters during a 24 hour period..
Haematological signs.  This refers to signs and symptoms relating to the haematological system..

Anaemia.  This refers to a reduction in the number of red blood cells, the amount of hemoglobin, and/or the volume of packed red blood cells. Common manifestations include pallor, fatigue, dizziness, shortness of breath, and tachycardia..
Neurological signs.  This refers to signs and symptoms relating to the neurological system..

Neck stiffness.  Defined as a sensation of tightness in the neck when attempting to move it, especially after a period of inactivity. Neck stiffness often involves soreness and difficulty moving the neck, especially when trying to turn the head to the side..

Hemiplegia.  This refers to severe or complete loss of motor function on one side of the body; often caused by brain diseases that are localized to the cerebral hemisphere opposite to the side of weakness; less frequently, brain stem lesions; cervical spinal cord diseases, peripheral nervous system diseases, and other conditions may manifest as hemiplegia..
Cognitive impairment.  This refers to diminished or impaired mental and/or intellectual function..

Psychological disturbance.  This refers to the presence of signs or symptoms that affect an individual's thoughts, emotions, behaviours or mental well-being. The presence of psychological disturbances should be identified through a Mental Status Examination (MSE) or equivalent tool..
Speech disturbance.  This refers to difficulties with speech and communication that may result from pathologies in the brain..

Agitation.  This refers to a state of excessive motor activity that is associated with mental distress or a feeling of substantial unease or inner tension. Distinguished from restlessness by the increased level of emotional distress and negative intensity of the experience. Agitation has a significant level of physical activity that is typically threatening to the self or others..

Cerebellar signs (cerebellar ataxia, incoordination, nystagmus).  Refers to the presence of a constellation of neurological signs typically indicate cerebellar dysfunction. Signs include dysdiadochokinesia, dysmetria, ataxia, nystagmus, intention tremor, slurred or scanning speech, hypotonia..
Other neurological abnormality.  This refers the presence of an alternative neurological abnormality not listed above..
Specify other neurological abnormality.  This refers the presence of another neurological abnormality not listed above..
Opthalmological signs.  This refers to signs and symptoms relating to the eye..
Retro-orbital pain.  Defined as the experience of pain in the retro-orbital region (behind the eyes)..
Subconjunctival haemorrhage.  Defined as the accumulation of blood underneath the conjunctiva, presenting as a bright red or dark patch in the eye..
Conjunctivitis.  Defined as inflammation of the conjunctiva.
Keratitis.  This refers to inflammation of the cornea of the eye..
Newly reduced visual acuity.  Defined as decreased clarity or sharpness of vision..
Sunken eyes.  This refers to an eye that is more deeply recessed into the plane of the face than is typical..
Other opthalmological signs.  This refers to other signs and symptoms relating to the eye, not specified above..
Specify other opthalmological signs.  This refers to other signs and symptoms relating to the eye, not specified above..
Paediatric-specific signs.  .
Nasal flaring.  This refers to widening of the nostrils during breathing, indicating increased respiratory effort..
Grunting.  This refers to a low-pitched expiratory sound produced during breathing to help maintain airway pressure and improve oxygenation..
Failure to thrive.  This refers to inadequate physical growth or failure to gain weight as expected for age..
Decreased tone / hypotonia.  This refers to decreased muscle tone resulting in reduced resistance to passive movement..
Bulging fontanelle.  This refers to outward bulging or fullness of the fontanelle due to increased intracranial pressure or other underlying pathology..
Other signs.  .
Other sign(s).  This refers to other signs and symptoms, not specified above..
Pregnant.  This refers to women who reports to be pregnant at presentation and/or have had a positive pregnancy test in recent days prior to presentation..
Post-partum (within 6 weeks of delivery).  This refers to the temporal period relating to mother from completion of labour until six weeks post-delivery..
Please complete the Pregnancy Form with information from the most recent pregnancy..  .

Gestational weeks at presentation.  This refers to the gestational age of the foetus (written in weeks). It can be calculated from the woman's last menstrual period (LMP) or calculated using the best obstetrical estimated due date (EDD) based on the following formula: Gestational Age = (280 - (EDD - Reference Date)). The reference date is the date in which you are trying to determine the gestational age..

Chorea: Involuntary, irregular, rapid, non-rhythmic movements that appear to flow randomly from one body part to another. Athetosis: Involuntary, slow, continuous, writhing movements, typically affecting the hands, fingers, feet, or toes. Dystonia: Sustained or intermittent involuntary muscle contractions causing abnormal, often repetitive movements or postures. Hemiballismus: Involuntary, large-amplitude, violent flinging movements affecting one side of the body. Stereotypies: Repetitive, purposeless, patterned movements or vocalizations that are performed in the same way each time. Orolingual dyskinesia: Involuntary, repetitive movements of the mouth, lips, jaw, or tongue. Tic: Sudden, rapid, recurrent, non-rhythmic motor movements or vocalizations that are difficult to suppress..

Rapid heart rate (tachycardia).  Refers to an abnormally rapid heart rate (typically > 100bpm for adults), that exceeds the range of the normal resting heart rate for age..
Cardiac arrhythmia.  Refers to an abnormality in rhythm of heartbeat, including rate, regularity, and/or sequence of activation abnormalities.
Peripheral cyanosis.  This refers to a condition of localized tissue damage due to pressure that obstructs blood flow to the skin and subcutaneous tissue..
Gastrointestinal signs.  This refers to signs and symptoms relating to the gastrointestinal system..
Ascites.  Defined as an excessive accumulation or retention of free fluid within the peritoneal cavity..
Palpable liver/Hepatomegaly.  Defined as an pathological enlargement of the liver.
Palpable spleen/splenomegaly.  Defined as an pathological enlargement of the spleen.
Tender abdomen.  This refers to painful sensation elicited upon touching the abdomen.
Jaundice.  Defined as a clinical manifestation of hyperbilirubinemia, characterized by the yellowish staining of the skin, mucous membrane and/or sclera..
Dark / tarry blood in faeces (melaena).  This refers to abnormally dark tarry feces containing blood, usually from gastrointestinal bleeding..

Fresh blood in stools (haematochezia).  This refers to the presence of blood in stool. It is the result of gastrointestinal hemorrhage and it may be easily seen in stool or may be identified microscopically..
Rectal bleeding.  This refers to bleeding originating from the rectal wall and discharged from the anus..
Feeding.  This refers to whether the patient is feeding or not.
If yes, specify feeding route, Options: Oral, Feeding tube, Breastfeeding.  If feeding, this refers to the route of feeding.
If no, nil per oral (NPO) order?.  This refers to clinical orders to indicate that nothing (e.g., medications, food) should be taken by mouth..
Haematological signs.  This refers to signs and symptoms relating to the haematological system..

Anaemia.  This refers to a reduction in the number of red blood cells, the amount of hemoglobin, and/or the volume of packed red blood cells. Common manifestations include pallor, fatigue, dizziness, shortness of breath, and tachycardia..
Neurological signs.  This refers to signs and symptoms relating to the neurological system..
Sedated/paralysed at time of assessment.  This refers to whether the patient was sedated or paralysed at the time of assessment.
Focal Neurology.  This refers to impairments of brain function, the nerve or spinal cord that affect a specific region of the body..

Specify focal neurology type, Options: Hemiparesis, Cranial nerve palsy, Aphasia, Visual field deficit, Movement disorder.  This refers to the type of focal neurological deficit. Hemiparesis refers to weakness affecting one side of the body. Cranial nerve palsy refers to loss or impairment of function of one or more cranial nerves. Aphasia refers to impairment of language affecting the ability to speak, understand, read, or write. Visual field deficit refers to partial or complete loss of vision within a portion of the normal visual field. Movement disorder refers to abnormal voluntary or involuntary movements resulting from impaired control of movement..

Type of movement disorder, Options: Tremor, Chorea, Dystonia, Myoclonus, Rigidity, Ataxia, Other.  This refers to the type of movement disorder. Tremor refers to an involuntary, rhythmic, oscillatory movement of a body part. Chorea refers to involuntary, irregular, rapid, non-rhythmic movements that appear to flow randomly from one body part to another. Dystonia refers to sustained or intermittent involuntary muscle contractions causing abnormal, often repetitive movements or postures. Myoclonus refers to sudden, brief, involuntary muscle jerks. Rigidity refers to increased resistance to passive movement that is present throughout the range of motion. Ataxia refers to impaired coordination of voluntary movements..
Seizures.  This refers to condition of involuntary abnormal motor, sensory, autonomic, or behavioural manifestations produced by irregular electrical activity in the brain..

Specify seizure type, Options: Clinical seizures, n-convulsive status epilepticus, EEG-confirmed seizure activity, Refractory status epilepticus.  This refers to the type of seizures. Clinical seizures refer to transient episodes of abnormal motor, sensory, autonomic, or behavioural manifestations. Non-convulsive status epilepticus refers to prolonged seizure activity with altered mental state in the absence of convulsions. EEG-confirmed seizure activity refers to seizure activity demonstrated by electroencephalography, with or without accompanying clinical manifestations. Refractory status epilepticus refers to status epilepticus that persists despite treatment with an adequate dose of a benzodiazepine and a second appropriate antiseizure medication..
Raised ICP.  This refers to raised intracranial pressure.

Specify raised ICP signs, Options: Cushing response, Papilloedema, Fixed/dilated pupil(s), Posturing.  This refers to specific clinical signs of raised intracranial pressure experienced by the patient. .

Encephalopathy.  This refers to a diffuse disruption of brain function and/or structure due to various causes including infection, metabolic disturbances, medication adverse effects, mass effects (e.g., from tumors), and radiation..

Specify encephalopathy phenotype, Options: Delirium (hyper/hypoactive), Behavioural disturbance, Psychosis, Coma.  This refers to the specific phenotype of encephalopathy. Delirium is characterized by impairments in attention and awareness (reduced orientation to the environment), as well as other cognitive disturbances (e.g., in memory, language, or perception). Behavioural disturbance refers to abnormal behavioural manuifestation with otherwise intact attention, awareness and cognition. Psychosis refers to an impaired perception of reality characterized by delusions, hallucinations, and/or disorganized thinking..

Neck stiffness.  Defined as a sensation of tightness in the neck when attempting to move it, especially after a period of inactivity. Neck stiffness often involves soreness and difficulty moving the neck, especially when trying to turn the head to the side..
Retro-orbital pain.  Defined as the experience of pain in the retro-orbital region (behind the eyes)..

Hemiplegia.  This refers to severe or complete loss of motor function on one side of the body; often caused by brain diseases that are localized to the cerebral hemisphere opposite to the side of weakness; less frequently, brain stem lesions; cervical spinal cord diseases, peripheral nervous system diseases, and other conditions may manifest as hemiplegia..
Cognitive impairment.  This refers to diminished or impaired mental and/or intellectual function..

Psychological disturbance.  This refers to the presence of signs or symptoms that affect an individual's thoughts, emotions, behaviours or mental well-being. The presence of psychological disturbances should be identified through a Mental Status Examination (MSE) or equivalent tool..
Speech disturbance.  This refers to difficulties with speech and communication that may result from pathologies in the brain..
Status epilepticus.  This refers to a condition of localized tissue damage due to pressure that obstructs blood flow to the skin and subcutaneous tissue..

Agitation.  This refers to a state of excessive motor activity that is associated with mental distress or a feeling of substantial unease or inner tension. Distinguished from restlessness by the increased level of emotional distress and negative intensity of the experience. Agitation has a significant level of physical activity that is typically threatening to the self or others..

Cerebellar signs (cerebellar ataxia, incoordination, nystagmus).  Refers to the presence of a constellation of neurological signs typically indicate cerebellar dysfunction. Signs include dysdiadochokinesia, dysmetria, ataxia, nystagmus, intention tremor, slurred or scanning speech, hypotonia..
Other neurological abnormality.  This refers the presence of an alternative neurological abnormality not listed above..
Specify other neurological abnormality.  This refers the presence of another neurological abnormality not listed above..
Opthalmological signs.  This refers to signs and symptoms relating to the eye..
Subconjunctival haemorrhage.  Defined as the accumulation of blood underneath the conjunctiva, presenting as a bright red or dark patch in the eye..
Conjunctivitis.  Defined as inflammation of the conjunctiva.
Keratitis.  This refers to inflammation of the cornea of the eye..
Newly reduced visual acuity.  Defined as decreased clarity or sharpness of vision..
Sunken eyes.  This refers to an eye that is more deeply recessed into the plane of the face than is typical..
Other opthalmological signs.  This refers to other signs and symptoms relating to the eye, not specified above..
Specify other opthalmological signs.  This refers to other signs and symptoms relating to the eye, not specified above..
Paediatric-specific signs.  .
Nasal flaring.  This refers to widening of the nostrils during breathing, indicating increased respiratory effort..
Grunting.  This refers to a low-pitched expiratory sound produced during breathing to help maintain airway pressure and improve oxygenation..
Failure to thrive.  This refers to inadequate physical growth or failure to gain weight as expected for age..
Decreased tone / hypotonia.  This refers to decreased muscle tone resulting in reduced resistance to passive movement..
Bulging fontanelle.  This refers to outward bulging or fullness of the fontanelle due to increased intracranial pressure or other underlying pathology..
Other  signs.  .
Other sign(s).  This refers the presence of an alternative sign(s) or symptom(s) not listed above..

Enter Treatments & Interventions data for this date?.  This section refers to treatments or interventions that are typically conducted and recorded in the emergency room and/or the ward or acute medical unit to which the patient was admitted between 00:00 and 24:00 hours on day of assessment..
Any fluids prescribed.  This refers to any prescribed fluids (oral or intravenous), excluding those the patient consumes in a non-prescribed dietary manner..
Oral rehydration.  This refers to oral (enteral) rehydration fluids, excluding those the patient consumes in a non-prescribed dietary manner..
Oral rehydration volume (mL/24 hours).  This refers to oral (enteral) rehydration fluids, excluding those the patient consumes in a non-prescribed dietary manner..

Intravenous (parenteral) fluids.  This refers to intravenous fluids, adminstered via a central or peripheral catheter into the venous system, for fluid resuscitation or replacement of electrolytes, calories, vitamins, or other medical reasons. Examples: 0.9% Sodium Chloride (Normal Saline), 5% Glucose (Dextrose 5% in Water), Albumin etc..

Intravenous fluid type.  This refers to intravenous fluids, adminstered via a central or peripheral catheter into the venous system, for fluid resuscitation or replacement of electrolytes, calories, vitamins, or other medical reasons. Examples: 0.9% Sodium Chloride (Normal Saline), 5% Glucose (Dextrose 5% in Water), Albumin etc..

Crystalloid volume (mL/24 hours).  Crystalloid intravenous fluids refer to aqueous solutions of mineral salts and other small, water-soluble molecules. They are commonly used for fluid replacement or resuscitation. Examples: 0.9% Sodium Chloride (Normal Saline), Lactated Ringer (USP), 5% Glucose (Dextrose 5% in Water) etc..

Colloid volume (mL/24 hours).  Colloid intravenous fluids are solutions containing large molecules, such as proteins or polysaccharides, which remain in the bloodstream for a longer duration compared and help maintain or expand intravascular volume. Examples: albumin, gelatin etc..

Blood / blood products transfusion.  This refers to a transfusion of whole blood or blood products such as packed red blood cells, platelets, fresh-frozen plasma, cryoprecipitate, fibrinogen concentrate, granulocytes etc. Excludes transfusion of human intravenous immunoglobulin..

Select all blood products that were administered., Options: Platelets, Cryoprecipitate, Whole blood, Frozen fresh plasma, Fibrigen concentrate, Packed RBC (red cell concentrate).  Platelets refers to the transfer of blood platelets from a donor to a recipient or reinfusion to the donor. Cryoprecipitate refers to a frozen blood product prepared from frozen plasma that contains fibrinogen (factor I), antihemophilic factor (factor VIII), factor XIII, von Willebrand factor (vWF) and fibronectin. Whole blood refers to intravenous administration of whole blood (blood that contains plasma and red blood cells) into an individual. Packed RBC refers to red blood cells from a unit of whole blood following removal of most of the plasma, leaving a unit with a haematocrit of about 6%. Fresh frozen plasma refers to the plasma that is separated from the whole blood and frozen quickly after a blood donation in order to be used for blood transfusions. Fibrinogen concentrate is a haemostatic agent used for the treatment of acute bleeding episodes in patients with congenital fibrinogen deficiency, including afibrinogenemia and hypofibrinogenemia..
Platelets (units/24 hours).  Platelets refers to the transfer of blood platelets from a donor to a recipient or reinfusion to the donor..

Cryoprecipitate (units/24 hours). Whole blood volume (units/24 hours).  Whole blood refers to intravenous administration of whole blood (blood that contains plasma and red blood cells) into an individual..

Frozen fresh plasma (units/24 hours).  Fresh frozen plasma refers to the plasma that is separated from the whole blood and frozen quickly after a blood donation in order to be used for blood transfusions..

Fibrinogen concentrate (units/24 hours).  Fibrinogen concentrate is a haemostatic agent used for the treatment of acute bleeding episodes in patients with congenital fibrinogen deficiency, including afibrinogenemia and hypofibrinogenemia..

Packed red blood cells (red cell concentrate) (units/24 hours).  Packed RBC refers to red blood cells from a unit of whole blood following removal of most of the plasma, leaving a unit with a haematocrit of about 6%..

Intravenous immunoglobulin.  This refers to immunoglobulin preparations, containing primarily Immunoglobulin G (IgG), that are used as intravenous infusions. Examples: Octagam®, Intragam P®, KIOVIG®, Flebogamma 5% DIF®, Carimune NF®, Gamunex®, Gammagard S/D®, Gammagard Liquid®, Gammaked® and Privigen®..

Plasmapheresis / plasma exchange.  Plasmapheresis (plasma exchange) refers to a procedure that separate and extracts plasma from the peripheral blood while returning the rest of the blood components to the donor..
Antibiotics.  Antibiotic refers to any agent(s) that selectively target bacteria. Topical preparations should not be recorded..

Corticosteroids.  Corticosteroids (commonly referred to as 'steroids') refers to all types of therapeutic corticosteroid, made in the adrenal cortex (the outer part of the adrenal gland). They are also made in the laboratory. Examples include: prednisolone, prednisone, methyl-prednisolone, dexamethasone, hydrocortisone, fluticasone, betametasone. Topical preparations are not included, but inhaled preparations are included..

Other intervention(s) or procedure(s).  Refers to treatment with corticosteroids via a delivery method that will affect the entire body (oral, intramuscular, intravenous or inhaled). Examples: prednisolone, prednisone, methyl-prednisolone, dexamethasone, hydrocortisone, fluticasone, betametasone. Topical preparations are not included..
Please specify other intervention(s) or procedure(s).  This refers to any other specific therapeutic intervention(s) or procedure(s) not otherwise characterised that you believe may be relevant..
Supplemental oxygen.  This refers to any method of oxygen therapy that may be delivered via nose cannula, mask or non-invasive or invasive ventilation..
Nasal prongs.  This refers to nasal prongs or nasal cannluae which deliver oxygen through two small prongs or cannulae insterted into the nostrils..
Face mask.  This refers to a simple oxygen face mask which is a device placed over a patient's nose, mouth, or tracheostomy to administer oxygen to the airway..

High flow nasal oxygen.  This refers to high -flow nasal oxygen therapy which is a non-invasive respiratory support that delivers warmed, humidified, oxygen-enriched air to patients at flow rates greater than those typically delivered by standard-flow oxygen devices..

Non-invasive ventilation.  This refers to non-invasive ventilation which provides ventilatory support through the patient's upper airway using a mask or similar device, without the need for tracheal intubation. Examples include Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) and Biphasic Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (BiPAP)..

Type of non-invasive ventilation, Options: CPAP, BIPAP, Other.  This refers to the type of non-invasive respiratory support or ventilation (NIV) used. Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) is a technique which uses a continuously maintains airway pressure above atmospheric pressure throughout the respiratory cycle to support spontaneous breathing activity. Biphasic Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (BPAP) uses a time-cycled change of the applied positive airway pressure level to support spontaneous breathing activity..

Any vasopressor / inotropic support.  This refers to continuous use of a vasopressor or inotrope for at least one hour. A vasopressor is a pharmaceutical agent that causes vasoconstriction. Examples: norepinephrine, epinephrine, vasopressin, terlipressin and phenylephrine. An inotrope is a pharmaceutical agent that alters the force of myocardial contractility. Examples of common 'positive' inotropes: dobutamine, dopamine, milrinone and epinephrine..

Reason for vasopressor / inotrope use, Options: Shock, Persistent hypotension, Other.  This refers to the reason for vasopressor or inotrope use. Shock is defined as circulatory failure with inadequate oxygen delivery to tissues and is assessed by measuring objective haemodynamic parameters, including pulse pressure, systolic blood pressure, and clinical sigs of hypoperfusion. A patient is classified as having shock if they meet the following objective haemodynamic markers: EITHER - pulse pressure <= 20mmHg or shock index (heart rate / SBP) >= 1.0 in adults and children > 5 years; OR SBP below absolute cutoffs: adults SBP < 90mmHg or MAP < 60; children < 1 year: SBP <70 mmHg; 1-10 years: SBP < [70 + (2 * age in years)]mmHg; > 10 years: SBP < 90mmHg; AND objective evidence of hypoperfusion with at least one of the following: peripheral CRT > 2s; urine output < 0.5 ml/kg/hr for >= 6 hours (if feasible); cold/clammy peripheries; or agitation or altered mental state. Persistent hypotension is confirmed when additional fluid boluses (>= 10ml/kg per bolus) or continuous IV fluids at >= 2 times maintenance rate are required (patients whose hypotension resolves after a single bolus or those with hypotension due to non-infectious causes (e.g. haemorrhage, cardiogenic shock) are excluded from this definition)..

New infiltrates present on X-ray, Options: bilateral, unilateral.  This refers to new pulmonary infiltrates present on the current chest x-ray, not visualised on previous chest radiographs of the patient. Pulmonary infiltrates result when a substance denser than air (e.g., pus, oedema, blood, surfactant, protein, or cells) is present within the lung parenchyma. Bilateral pulmonary infiltrates are present in both lungs. Unilateral pulmonary infiltrates are present in one lung only..

Infiltrates on X-ray consistent with, Options: Viral pneumonitis, Bacterial pneumonia, Pulmonary oedema.  This refers to the pathological condition with which the pulmonary infiltrates on chest x-ray may be consistent with. Viral pneumonitis characteristically produces bilateral perihilar peribronchial thickening and interstitial infiltrates which, particularly in children, due to their small-calibre airways, can result in areas of atelectasis or air trapping. Bacterial pneumonia characteristically produces focal segmental (i.e. bronchopneumonia) or lobar pulmonary opacities (i.e. lobar pneumonia). Pulmonary oedema may be characterised by cephalisation of upper lobe vessels, interstitial opacities, peribronchovascular cuffing, septal lines (Kerley B lines), airspace opacification (filling of the alveoli with fluid) which can have a perihilar or 'batwing' distribution when severe and acute; and pleural effusion..

CT brain findings, Options: Cerebral oedema, Midline shift, Hydrocephalus, Intracranial hemorrhage, Infarction.  This refers to the findings of the CT Brain scan. Cerebral oedema is the abnormal accumulation of fluid within the brain parenchyma and on CT, it appears as hypoattenuation with compression and displacement of adjacent structures. Midline shift is a finding described on transverse (axial) slices from CT scans where the midline of the intracranial anatomy is no longer in the midline and is the result of pushing or pulling forces within either side of the intracranial compartment. Hydrocephalus is the abnormal enlargement of the cerebral ventricles due to impaired cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) circulation, absorption, or, overproduction and on CT it shows ventricular dilatation, often with enlarged temporal horns and periventricular low attenuation (transependymal CSF seepage) in acute hydrocephalus. Intracranial haemorrhage is characterised by the extravascular accumulation of blood within different intracranial spaces and on CT, blood appears markedly hyperdense compared to brain parenchyma. Cerebral infarction refers to death of brain tissue due to loss of blood supply. .

Midline shift (mm).  Midline shift is a finding described on transverse (axial) slices from CT scans where the midline of the intracranial anatomy is no longer in the midline and is the result of pushing or pulling forces within either side of the intracranial compartment. Midline shift is measured in millimetres, as the perpendicular distance between a midline structure (usually the septum pellucidum) and a line designated the midline. The midline is assumed to be coplanar with the falx cerebri and is best represented as a line drawn between the anterior and posterior attachments of the falx to the inner table of the skull..

Ascites grading, Options: Small, Moderate, Severe. Biospecimen type, SampleType: Amniotic fluid.  This refers to the type of a clinical specimen collected for pathogen testing. Nasal / Nasopharyngeal (NP) swab refers to collection biological material from within the nasal passages/nasopharynx. Throat swab refers to collection biological material from within the throat/oropharynx. Combined nasal/NP + throat swab refers to collection using both nasal / nasopharyngeal (NP) swab and throat swab. Sputum refers to material coughed up from the lungs and expectorated via the mouth. Bronchoalveolar Lavage (BAL) refers to washing out of the lungs with saline or mucolytic agents for diagnostic or therapeutic purposes. Endotracheal aspirate (ETA) refers to collection of specimen from endotracheal tube. Eye swab refers to collection of biological sample from the surface of the eye. Lesion swab refers to collection of biological sample from a lesion on the skin or mucous membrane. Semen refers to the secretion of male reproductive organs discharged upon ejaculation. Faeces / rectal swab refers to biological sample collected from faecal matter or from the rectum by swabbing..
